excerpt: The China Jinping Underground Laboratory, inaugurated in 2010, is an underground research facility ... the deepest rock overburden and largest space by volume in the world. ... Phase II of the facility is being constructed. Sec. II: "Construction of Phase I of CJPL (CJPL-I) started in December 2009 near the center of one of the Jinping traffic tunnels, where the vertical rock overburden is maximal... It has drive-in access via a two-lane road tunnel... (The distances to the east and west ends of the tunnel entrance are 8.7 km and 8.8 km, respectively.)" Table I: CJPL-I volume 4,000 m^3, rock burden/depth 2,400 m, start year 2010; CJPL-II volume 300,000 m^3, rock burden/depth 2,400 m, start year 2017. Sec. VI: "CJPL-II is located 500 m to the west of CJPL-I, along the same road tunnel. It will have four caverns, each with dimensions of 14 m (width) x 14 m (height) x 130 m (length)..." Table III: main road tunnels, two parallel tunnels, 9.2(8.3) km from east(west) entrance [to CJPL-II].
title: The China Jinping Underground Laboratory and its Early Science
